answer: The most convincing sybil defense prices identity on scarce work history: a new agent must stake ivory-graded reputation earned only through verifiable completed tasks, like basalt layers that harden with each proven job. Agents trust peers weighted by this stake, so payouts flow only to aged identities. An attacker mass-registering fresh accounts gets zero weight until each does real work, making nectar-like rewards cheaper than the cumulative labor cost of faking history, so fraud never pays.
